title: U.S. House · Texas's 15th District
area: South Texas's Rio Grande Valley, including parts of Hidalgo and surrounding counties around Edinburg and McAllen.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Monica De La Cruz won her primary unopposed. Bobby Pulido, a Tejano musician and small-business owner, defeated Ada Cuellar in the Democratic primary, 67.5%-32.5%. Texas's 2025 redistricting changed roughly 80% of the district's territory from the version De La Cruz has represented since 2023; as of late September 2026, election forecasters rated the general election from Lean Republican (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk) to Tilt Republican (Inside Elections) to Toss-up (Sabato's Crystal Ball). As of June 30, 2026, De La Cruz had raised $5.27 million to Pulido's $2.96 million.

candidates.name: Monica De La Cruz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Monica De La Cruz is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 15th District, which was redrawn in 2025. A Brownsville native and former insurance agency owner, she lost the 2020 race, won the seat in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024. She serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services committees, and her campaign website says she has secured passage of five pieces of legislation, including a fentanyl-trafficking bill.

background.text: De La Cruz was born in Brownsville, Texas, in 1974, and graduated from James Pace Early College High School there.
She earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Texas at San Antonio in 1997.
Before running for office she owned and operated an insurance agency and worked as an insurance agent.
She won the July 14, 2020 Republican runoff over Ryan Krause for the 15th District nomination, then lost the November 2020 general election to Democratic incumbent Vicente Gonzalez Jr.
She was first elected to the House in 2022, defeating Democrat Michelle Vallejo, and won re-election against Vallejo in 2024 after winning that year's Republican primary over Vangela Churchill.
She serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services committees.
In March 2024 she delivered the Republican response to President Biden's State of the Union address in Spanish.

Her House website describes her as the first Republican Latina to represent Texas in Congress and says she has passed three major pieces of legislation into law and resolved nearly 1,500 constituent cases; her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, cites five pieces of legislation, including the first bill in nearly 20 years from her community to be signed into law, targeting fentanyl trafficking.

Texas adopted a new congressional map in 2025; a University of Texas at San Antonio professor quoted by Ballotpedia said about 80% of the redrawn 15th District is territory she has not represented in the last two election cycles.

priorities.text: Border security, described by her campaign as a central focus of her time in office.
South Texas agriculture and water: created the South Texas Water Working Group and says she is pressing the Mexican government to meet water-treaty obligations to the region.

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Agriculture as Vice Chair of its Subcommittee on Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture, and on its Subcommittee on General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves as Vice Chair of the Committee on Financial Services for the 119th Congress.

Her campaign says she secured passage of five pieces of legislation during her time in office, including a bill targeting fentanyl trafficking that her campaign describes as the first bill from her community signed into law in nearly 20 years.

candidates.name: Bobby Pulido
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 67.5%-32.5%, over Ada Cuellar

summary.text: Bobby Pulido is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Monica De La Cruz in Texas's 15th District. An Edinburg native, he has been a Tejano recording artist for about three decades and describes himself as a small-business owner and father of four. He is running on affordability, water infrastructure, public education and comprehensive immigration reform, and won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Ada Cuellar.

background.text: Pulido was born in Edinburg, Texas, in 1973, the oldest child of Tejano singer Roberto Pulido, and graduated from Edinburg High School.
He was accepted at St. Mary's University, where he studied political science, before leaving college to pursue a singing career.
He debuted with his own band in 1995 and signed with EMI Latin; his debut album Desvelado was certified platinum by the RIAA.

The Texas Tribune describes him as known for 1990s hits including "Desvelado" and "Se Murió de Amor", a five-time Latin Grammy nominee and 22-time Tejano Music Award nominee who won eight times early in his career.
He has also acted, including a lead role in the 2003 television film La Decada Furiosa.
According to his campaign website, he has run businesses and created jobs in South Texas; Ballotpedia lists his career as musician and small business owner.
He announced a run for Congress in September 2025, after forming an exploratory committee that July, to challenge De La Cruz.
Pulido won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Ada Cuellar with 67.5% of the vote.
According to his campaign website, he is a father of four.

priorities.text: Public education: opposes private-school voucher programs and wants higher teacher pay and reduced classroom overcrowding.
Water infrastructure: supports investment in desalination and modern irrigation to address the Rio Grande Valley's water shortage, and wants Mexico held to its water-treaty obligations.
Affordability, including lowering costs for families and small businesses.

positions.summary: Says he opposes voucher programs that he says drain money from public classrooms and send it to private schools.
